key_insight: SHADE enables federated unlearning of quantum data by replacing replay with classical shadows that estimate each forgotten state's training influence and subtract it via a federated Newton correction.
engineering_relevance: This makes quantum federated learning practical for edge and sensor networks where quantum data cannot be cloned or remeasured after training.
method: Record a classical shadow for every training quantum state using randomized single-qubit measurements.
Use shadow-based estimates of gradients and curvature at the current QNN parameters for the forget set.
Apply a federated Newton-style correction so only classical summaries, not quantum states, move across nodes.
evidence_signal: In simulation with 50 nodes and on edge boards, SHADE matches retraining-level forget accuracy within 0.5 points and runs in under 0.2 s.
watch_item: Shadow size can grow exponentially with the backward light cone of the measured observable, so measurement locality strongly affects scalability.
paper_title: Federated Unlearning of Quantum Data via Classical Shadows
